name: GRAND
notes: detector:grand is placed at site:grandproto300-dunhuang, the nearest named city to GRANDProto300's actual location ('200 km^2 in the Gobi Desert near Xiaodushan, in northern Dunhuang, China' per the collaboration's own progress paper) -- no fetched source states a numeric latitude/longitude for the array itself, so the city point is used as a coarse regional pointer (kind: campus, confidence: uncertain) rather than a surveyed position, per A17's fallback rule.

Three small-scale prototype arrays exist since 2023 per the 2026 JINST paper: GRAND@Nancay (France), GRAND@Auger (Argentina) and GRANDProto300 (China); only GRANDProto300 is modelled in any detail here since it is the collaboration's own most-covered prototype in the sources fetched.
No INSPIRE experiment-registry lookup was performed for GRAND in this session; external.inspire_experiment left null.
Derived fields (detector_ids, site_ids, result_ids, document_ids) are deliberately not written (v0.2 A1).

physics_goals.quote: planned large-scale observatory: 20 separate, independent sub-arrays, each of 10,000 radio antennas deployed over 10,000 km^2, for a total of 200,000 antennas
physics_goals.value: Detect ultra-high-energy cosmic neutrinos and cosmic rays using giant radio antenna arrays sensitive to air showers and Earth-skimming neutrino-induced showers

summary.plain: A giant planned array of 200,000 radio antennas spread over a huge area, designed to catch the radio flash from ultra-high-energy cosmic rays and neutrinos. Small test versions are already up and running in China, France and Argentina.
summary.technical: Planned 200,000-antenna, 20-sub-array giant radio observatory for ultra-high-energy neutrinos and cosmic rays. The full design array remains at the proposal stage, but the GRANDProto300 prototype in the Gobi Desert near Dunhuang, China has been deployed and growing since June 2023 (13-antenna stage, then 65-antenna stage by April 2025), alongside sister prototypes GRAND@Nancay (France) and GRAND@Auger (Argentina), all operating since 2023.
